title: Thinking in Tailwind
summary: Utility classes, responsive and state variants, and composing class names in components.

steps.title: Utility classes
body: **Tailwind CSS** replaces writing CSS rules with small, single-purpose classes applied directly in markup:

Reading the names: `p-4` padding (4 x 0.25rem = 1rem), `mt-2` margin-top, `text-lg` font size, `text-gray-600` colour, `rounded-lg` border radius, `flex items-center gap-2` a flex row with centred items and spacing.

Why it works for component code: the styles live **with** the component, nothing leaks between components, and you never invent class names. The spacing and colour **scale** keeps designs consistent. Tailwind scans your source for class names and generates only the CSS you use, so class names must appear as **complete strings** (`"bg-red-500"`, never `"bg-" + color + "-500"`).
> **Try it:** in the **Playground**'s HTML/CSS/JS tab, turn on the **Tailwind** switch and paste the card above.

steps.title: Variants: responsive, state, dark
body: A prefix applies a utility only in some condition:

- **Responsive**: `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:` mean "at this width **and up**". Tailwind is **mobile first**: unprefixed classes are for small screens, and prefixes override them on bigger ones. `grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3` is one column on phones, three from medium screens.
In React you build the class string from props. A tiny helper, often called `cn` or `clsx`, joins the truthy parts:
<button className={cn("px-3 py-2 rounded", primary ? "bg-blue-600 text-white" : "bg-gray-100", disabled && "opacity-50")} />

steps.prompt: `class="text-sm md:text-lg"`: what size is the text on a phone and on a wide desktop?
options: small on the phone, large on the desktop
large on the phone, small on the desktop
steps.explain: Mobile first: the unprefixed class applies everywhere, and `md:` overrides it from the medium breakpoint up.

steps.prompt: Will Tailwind generate the CSS for it?
buckets: yes: complete class names in source
steps.explain: Tailwind reads your files as text and looks for whole class names. Map variants to complete strings.

steps.title: A cn helper
prompt: Write `cn(...parts)` that joins class names with single spaces. Each part may be a string, `false`, `null`, `undefined`, or an object whose keys are included when their value is truthy. Extra whitespace inside strings is collapsed and empty parts are skipped.
cn("px-3  py-2", false, { "opacity-50": true, hidden: false }, undefined, " rounded ")
starter: type ClassPart = string | false | null | undefined | Record<string, boolean | undefined>;
solution: type ClassPart = string | false | null | undefined | Record<string, boolean | undefined>;
else for (const [name, on] of Object.entries(part)) if (on) out.push(name);
template: Dojo.eq("mixed parts", "px-3 py-2 opacity-50 rounded", cn("px-3  py-2", false, { "opacity-50": true, hidden: false }, undefined, " rounded "));

steps.title: Button variants
prompt: Write `buttonClass({ variant, size, disabled })` returning the class string for a button, built from **complete** class names:
- variant `"primary"`: `"bg-blue-600 text-white hover:bg-blue-700"`; `"secondary"`: `"bg-gray-100 text-gray-900 hover:bg-gray-200"`; `"danger"`: `"bg-red-600 text-white hover:bg-red-700"`
- size `"sm"`: `"px-2 py-1 text-sm"`; `"md"` (default): `"px-4 py-2"`; `"lg"`: `"px-6 py-3 text-lg"`
Parts appear in that order, joined by single spaces. `variant` defaults to `"primary"`.
starter: type ButtonProps = { variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "danger"; size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg"; disabled?: boolean };
function buttonClass({ variant = "primary", size = "md", disabled = false }: ButtonProps): string {
solution: type ButtonProps = { variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "danger"; size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg"; disabled?: boolean };
const sizes = { sm: "px-2 py-1 text-sm", md: "px-4 py-2", lg: "px-6 py-3 text-lg" } as const;
function buttonClass({ variant = "primary", size = "md", disabled = false }: ButtonProps): string {
return ["inline-flex items-center rounded font-medium", variants[variant], sizes[size], disabled && "opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed"]
template: Dojo.eq("defaults", "inline-flex items-center rounded font-medium bg-blue-600 text-white hover:bg-blue-700 px-4 py-2", buttonClass({}));

Dojo.eq("danger lg disabled", "inline-flex items-center rounded font-medium bg-red-600 text-white hover:bg-red-700 px-6 py-3 text-lg opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed", buttonClass({ variant: "danger", size: "lg", disabled: true }));
Dojo.eq("secondary sm", "inline-flex items-center rounded font-medium bg-gray-100 text-gray-900 hover:bg-gray-200 px-2 py-1 text-sm", buttonClass({ variant: "secondary", size: "sm" }));

hints: Keep lookup objects `variants` and `sizes` with complete strings.
